title: US STOCKS-Wall St drops on tariff worries, with Apple in crosshairs
text:
Shutterstock photo
(For a live blog on the U.S. stock market, click LIVE/ ortype LIVE/ in an Eikon news window.)
* Trump: tariffs ready on $267 bln worth of Chinese imports
* Payroll numbers strong but raise inflation worries
* Tesla stalls on executive departures, Musk webcast
* Indexes down: Dow 0.31 pct, S&P 0.22 pct, Nasdaq 0.25 pct (New throughout, updates prices, market activity and commentsto close)
By April Joyner
NEW YORK, Sept 7 (Reuters) - Wall Street's major indexesfell on Friday as U.S. President Donald Trump raised thepossibility of additional tariffs on Chinese imports and AppleInc AAPL.O indicated that some of its products could besubjected to such levies.
U.S. stocks were lower for most of Friday's session butdipped further in the last half-hour of trading on reports thatApple products, including the Apple Watch and AirPods, would beslapped with duties. Apple shares, which had been in positiveterritory for most of the session, ended 0.8 percent lower. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL3N1VT5C5
The company provided those details in response to the WhiteHouse's proposed tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chineseimports. A comment period for those tariffs ended on Thursdaynight. Earlier on Friday, White House economic adviser LarryKudlow said Trump would not make any decisions on those tariffsuntil officials evaluated public comments. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL2N1VT0U5
"Apple is a bellwether name," said Quincy Krosby, chiefmarket strategist at Prudential Financial in Newark, New Jersey."(That's) why we may be seeing some profit-taking going into theweekend."
U.S. stocks had already been pressured after Trump said hehad tariffs ready to impose on an additional $267 billion worthof Chinese imports, on top of the proposed $200 billion.
The escalated trade rhetoric contributed to anxiety amonginvestors regarding the market's outlook.
"There's the possibility of (China) devaluing its currencyagain, which pushes up the dollar and turns the pressure up onU.S. exporters," Krosby said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI fell 79.33 points,or 0.31 percent, to 25,916.54, the S&P 500 .SPX lost 6.37points, or 0.22 percent, to 2,871.68 and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC dropped 20.19 points, or 0.25 percent, to 7,902.54.
For the week, the Dow lost 0.19 percent, the S&P fell 1.03percent, and the Nasdaq shed 2.55 percent. The Nasdaq registeredits greatest weekly percentage decline since late March, whilethe S&P's weekly percentage drop was its biggest since lateJune.
The S&P and Dow had opened lower after the U.S. LaborDepartment's employment report showed accelerating job growthand a surge in wage growth. Though the report indicated a strongeconomy, it raised concerns among investors regarding inflationand the Federal Reserve's plans for increasing interest rates. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nLNS7KEEK1
With the added pressures from trade concerns, 10 out of theS&P's 11 major sectors ended lower. Only health care .SPXHC stocks posted gains.
Shares of chipmaker Broadcom IncAVGO.O rose 7.7 percentafter a strong current-quarter revenue forecast. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL3N1VS5XF
Tesla IncTSLA.O shares slid 6.3 percent following reportsof two executives leaving the company and on mounting investorconcerns about Chief Executive Elon Musk's behavior after hesmoked marijuana on a live Web show. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL3N1VT4L2
Declining issues outnumbered advancing ones on the NYSE by a2.21-to-1 ratio; on Nasdaq, a 1.24-to-1 ratio favored decliners.
The S&P 500 posted 37 new 52-week highs and 16 new lows; theNasdaq Composite recorded 99 new highs and 66 new lows.
Volume on U.S. exchanges was 6.25 billion shares, comparedto the 6.2 billion average over the last 20 trading days.
